chunks: Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz narrated to me from Ibn Abi al-Khattab, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Mudarib from Malik al-Juhani from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: O Malik! When Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, took the life of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), He sent to him four thousand angels, disheveled and covered with dust, who weep for him until the Day of Judgment.
So whoever visits him, knowing his right, Allah will forgive him his past and future sins, and record for him a Hajj.
And he will remain protected until he returns to his family.

He said: So when Malik died and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) passed away, I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him of the hadith. When I reached the mention of 'Hajj', he said: 'And an Umrah, O Muhammad!'

key_terms.شُعْثاً غُبْراً: Disheveled and covered with dust (state of angels)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam al-Husayn's shrine according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the cosmic significance of Imam al-Husayn’s martyrdom, noting that four thousand angels weep for him until the Day of Judgment, a testament to his elevated spiritual status in Shia theology. It establishes the theological basis for *Ziyarat* as an act of worship that grants complete forgiveness of sins and counts as a Hajj (and Umrah, as clarified by Imam al-Sadiq), ensuring divine protection for the pilgrim. This underscores the concept of *Haqq al-Husayn* (the right of Husayn) as a means of intercession and spiritual purification.
